status_summary: The Fed's statutory mandate is unchanged, but a bill to remove the maximum-employment goal has cleared a House committee. H.R. 5396, the Price Stability Act (Rep. Hill, chairman of the House Financial Services Committee; introduced 2025-09-16), amends section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act to remove the employment goal while leaving the moderate long-term interest rates goal in place. The committee ordered the bill reported by a 30 to 21 vote on 2026-05-13 and reported it with an amendment on 2026-06-24 (H. Rept. 119-710, Union Calendar No. 616); no House floor vote or Senate companion was found, and a CRS product of 2026-05-21 discusses only this bill. Separately, the FOMC reaffirmed its longer-run goals statement on 2026-01-27 with both maximum employment and price stability and a 2 percent goal; that statement, unchanged from August 2025, no longer contains averaging language, so the Fed itself dropped the flexible average inflation targeting approach the chapter wanted ended (an action by the Fed, not by elected officials). The FOMC's 2026-09-16 statement describes its rate increase as supporting the dual mandate. Kevin Warsh was sworn in as chair on 2026-05-22, and on 2026-07-09 the Fed announced task forces, including one on inflation frameworks. No statutory requirement for a published inflation target range and path was found.

timeline.event: Rep. Hill, with Reps. Stutzman and Donalds, introduces H.R. 5396, the Price Stability Act, which amends section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act to remove the maximum-employment goal; referred to the House Financial Services Committee. The committee's release of 2025-09-17 describes it as ending the dual mandate.
FOMC reaffirmed its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy with text unchanged from August 2025 (reaffirmation at the annual organization meeting).
House Financial Services Committee holds a markup of H.R. 5396 and orders it reported with an amendment by a recorded vote of 30 to 21, per the bill status record.
Kevin Warsh sworn in as Fed chairman and Board member and selected as FOMC chairman; nominated 2026-03-04 and confirmed by the Senate 2026-05-12 (Board) and 2026-05-13 (chair).

H.R. 5396 reported with an amendment by the Committee on Financial Services (H. Rept. 119-710) and placed on the Union Calendar (No. 616); the reported version is titled the Price Stability Act of 2026.
Fed announced five task forces to review the conduct of monetary policy, including inflation frameworks (co-led by N. Gregory Mankiw, Thomas Sargent and William White) and communications.
FOMC statement raised the target range by 0.25 percentage point and described the action as supporting the Fed's dual mandate; vote 12 to 0.
